transcript.text: quick q: churn with 3% positives, should i report PR-AUC or ROC-AUC to my manager, and why? no data work, just the answer

Report **PR-AUC**, with ROC-AUC as a footnote. Why: with only 3% positives, ROC-AUC is flattered by the huge number of easy negatives — a model can look strong on it while catching almost no real churners. PR-AUC scores precision and recall on the rare class, so it moves only when your model actually finds churners. For your manager, pair it with one plain number: what share of churners you catch, and how many false alarms that costs. That's the decision they care about; a single AUC number, whichever one, doesn't tell them that.
